problem.symptom: 8K writes a non-decodable video track; 4K120 and sustained/long 4K60 abort MPEG4Writer with a FORTIFY write overflow (SIGABRT) about three seconds in, so no file and no thermal curve.
problem.cause: The Xiaomi HEVC recorder enables vendor.qti-ext-enc-nal-length-bs (num-bytes=4), so the vendor encoder emits length-prefixed NAL units (a 4-byte big-endian length before each NAL) instead of Annex-B start codes. MPEG4Writer's HEVC/AVC sample path (addMultipleLengthPrefixedSamples_l via getNextNALUnit) scans for 0x00000001 start codes. A NAL length in [256,511] is 00 00 01 xx, which looks like a 3-byte start code, so the parser misframes: with no real start code it writes the whole AU as one sample (non-decodable), and a false split makes nextNalStart - currentNalStart - 4 underflow to (size_t)-1, which the file write rejects with FORTIFY: write: count 18446744073709551615 > SSIZE_MAX.

fix.call_site: MPEG4Writer::Track sample loop, immediately before StripStartcode(copy) for usePrefix (AVC/HEVC) tracks
fix.mechanism: Per access unit: if the buffer is exactly a chain of 4-byte length-prefixed NAL units, validated end to end (each length >= 2, fits the buffer, consumes the buffer exactly, and every NAL has forbidden_zero_bit == 0), rewrite each 4-byte length prefix in place as a 4-byte Annex-B start code (00 00 00 01). The existing, tested Annex-B logic (StripStartcode, addMultipleLengthPrefixedSamples_l, sample-size accounting) then handles it unchanged.
fix.gate: Self-validating per-buffer detection; no format-key plumbing. Only activates when the whole AU parses as length-prefixed. Annex-B input starts with a start code and never validates, so normal encoders are untouched.
fix.does_not_touch: Codec-specific data (hvcc/csd) path is unchanged; short 4K60 and 1080p already record and play, proving the csd is Annex-B.
fix.safety: A false positive would corrupt normal recording, so detection is strict; a 20000-buffer random Annex-B fuzz produced zero false positives (tests/test_hevc_length_prefixed.py). A false negative only reproduces the pre-existing bug.

remaining: On-device confirmation that 8K, 4K120 and long 4K60 record decodable tracks with no MPEG4Writer abort
Whether 8K/120fps sustain thermally and at the encoder's real bitrate is a separate question from the writer fix
